task.description:
Design a fix for GH #520 / ISS-0186: TC-EXP-301-05 (tests/integration/effects_subsystem_test.zig, block starting ~line 570) asserts on a measured wall-clock delta between two separate database reads (next_attempt_at read BEFORE markRetry, then read AFTER, subtracting to get observed_delta_ms, compared against expected_ms +/- 500ms tolerance at lines 689-694). Root cause: Queue.markRetry (src/effects/queue.zig:84-108) computes next_attempt_at = NOW() + $3::interval entirely on the PostgreSQL server side using SQL NOW() -- the Zig test has no control over or synchronized view of that server clock, and under ~20-test-binaries-concurrent load (zig build test-integration-svc), scheduling jitter between the test's two separate query round-trips exceeds the +/-500ms tolerance. Design a fix that asserts a deterministic property instead: read next_attempt_at AND a server-side NOW() snapshot in the SAME query (single round-trip, e.g. SELECT EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM next_attempt_at)*1000, EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM NOW())*1000 in one statement, executed once, immediately after markRetry returns) so there is no cross-round-trip jitter window at all -- the interval between next_attempt_at and that same query's NOW() should equal the requested backoff_ms exactly (modulo query execution time within a single round trip, which is sub-millisecond, not the multi-hundred-ms cross-request jitter the current two-round-trip design is vulnerable to). Alternatively/additionally consider asserting the raw interval algebraically: since next_attempt_at = t_exec + backoff_ms where t_exec is the server's own NOW() at execution time, capturing BOTH values in one query removes the wall-clock-relative-to-test-process measurement entirely. Read the current test block in full (tests/integration/effects_subsystem_test.zig around lines 567-696) and src/effects/queue.zig's markRetry before designing. The acceptance criteria require the assertion still fails on a genuine backoff-schedule regression -- do not weaken it into a tautology (e.g. do not just assert next_attempt_at > NOW() with no bound).

REWORK 1:
- [BLOCKER] Tolerance justification is factually wrong for this codebase. TC-EXP-301-05 runs entirely inside TestHarness.init()'s single explicit conn.begin() (tests/integration/helpers.zig:1085) held open until deinit()'s rollback -- both markRetry's UPDATE and the follow-up SELECT execute on the SAME &h.conn inside that ONE already-open transaction (vendor/pg/pg.zig:149-161 confirms Conn.exec/Conn.query never issue implicit per-call BEGIN/COMMIT). Per PostgreSQL semantics, NOW() is frozen at transaction start and identical for every statement in that transaction, so next_attempt_at and a follow-up NOW() read are the SAME value read twice, not two independently-drifting values. Re-derive the tolerance -- likely 0.0ms or a tiny client-side float round-trip epsilon (EXTRACT/parseFloat), not the proposed 50ms.
acceptance_criteria: Design replaces the two-separate-query wall-clock delta measurement with a single-round-trip deterministic assertion
The assertion still fails if the backoff schedule regresses -- not weakened into a tautology
Design is implementable as a test-only change (tests/integration/effects_subsystem_test.zig) with no production code touched
No implementation code present in the design artefact

result.summary: Reworked design to correct the PostgreSQL transaction-semantics claim the validator flagged as BLOCKER. Verified against source: TC-EXP-301-05 runs entirely inside TestHarness.init()'s single conn.begin() (helpers.zig:1085), held open until deinit()'s rollback() (helpers.zig:1147); every statement in the test (seed-loop markRetry, pre-check read, markRetry, read-back) executes on the same &h.conn with no begin()/commit()/rollback() calls of its own; Conn.exec/Conn.query (pg.zig:149-174) never issue implicit per-call BEGIN/COMMIT. So markRetry's UPDATE and the read-back SELECT share ONE transaction, and NOW() (= transaction_timestamp()) is frozen and identical for both -- not two independently-drifting autocommit reads. Re-derived tolerance from 50ms down to 1.0ms: a client-side float round-trip epsilon (EXTRACT(EPOCH...)*1000 through float8, then parseFloat), not a timing/jitter budget, since the underlying comparison is now exact server-side arithmetic. Also reconciled why the original two-read test was ever flaky: both old reads shared the same frozen NOW(), so it cancelled out of the old delta entirely -- the old ±500ms tolerance was actually masking a comparison-correctness gap (the 'before' value depended on the seed loop's prior write, not cleanly on i), not absorbing real jitter. Kept the non-tautology structure, the four expected_backoff values, and test-only scope unchanged. tools/lint_design_artefact.py exits 0, no BLOCKER/MAJOR.
